what_is.title: What is a Liver Transplant?
what_is.description: A liver transplant is a life-saving surgery where a diseased or damaged liver is removed and replaced with a healthy liver from a donor. This operation is usually recommended when the liver can no longer perform its essential functions.
what_is.description2: The liver is one of the body’s most important organs – it filters toxins, produces proteins, stores nutrients, and aids digestion. When the liver stops working due to disease, conditions like<bold> liver failure, cirrhosis, or liver cancer </bold>can develop. In such cases, a liver transplant may be the only option to restore health and quality of life.

why_needed.title: Why is a Liver Transplant Needed?
why_needed.description: Doctors may recommend a liver transplant when other treatments fail. Common reasons include:
why_needed.cirrhosisDes1: The most common cause of liver transplants.
why_needed.cirrhosisDes2: Results from scarring of liver tissue due to <bold>hepatitis B or C, alcohol abuse, or fatty liver disease.</bold>
why_needed.acute_failureDes1: A sudden loss of liver function, often caused by <bold>viral infections, medication overdoses (like paracetamol), or autoimmune diseases.</bold>
why_needed.acute_failureDes2: Can be life-threatening and requires urgent transplant.
why_needed.cancerDes1: When confined to the liver and not spread to other organs.
why_needed.cancerDes2: Transplant removes both the cancer and the diseased liver.
why_needed.pediatricDes: Children born with<bold> biliary atresia </bold>(blocked bile ducts) often need a transplant.
why_needed.geneticDes: Conditions such as<bold> Wilson’s disease, hemochromatosis, or alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency</bold> may damage the liver and require transplantation.

types.title: Types of Liver Transplants
types.living_donor_point1: A healthy donor gives a portion of their liver to the patient.
types.living_donor_point2: The liver regenerates in both donor and recipient.
types.living_donor_point3: Reduces waiting time, especially in countries like India with donor shortages.
types.deceased_donor_point1: The liver is taken from a brain-dead donor whose other organs still function.
types.othersPoint1: <bold>Auxiliary Transplant: </bold>Partial donor liver transplanted while part of patient’s own liver remains.
types.othersPoint2: <bold>Pediatric Transplant:</bold> Specially designed for children with liver disorders.

recovery.title: Recovery After Liver Transplant
recovery.diet: Eat a healthy diet (no alcohol, low salt)

risks.title: Risks & Complications of Liver Transplant
risks.Description: Like any major surgery, risks exist:
risks.rare: <bold>Rare:</bold> Bile duct leaks, blood clots, graft failure
risks.long_term: <bold>Long-term:</bold> Chronic rejection, higher risk of cancers due to immunosuppressants

kidney_transplant.title: Kidney Transplant Surgery in India – Procedure, Benefits, Risks & Recovery
kidney_transplant.intro_para1: Learn everything about<bold> kidney transplant surgery in India</bold> – what it is, why it’s needed, indications, eligibility, procedure, risks, recovery process, and donor options.InDocsCare connects you with top kidney transplant hospitals and expert surgeons at affordable costs.
kidney_transplant.what_is_para1: <bold>A kidney transplant</bold> is a surgical procedure in which a healthy kidney from a living or deceased donor is placed into a patient whose kidneys have lost the ability to function properly.This treatment is often recommended for patients with<bold> end-stage renal disease (ESRD) or advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD).</bold>
kidney_transplant.what_is_para2: Healthy kidneys filter toxins and waste products, balance electrolytes, control blood pressure, and regulate body fluids.When the kidneys fail, toxins build up in the body, leading to life-threatening complications.A kidney transplant restores these vital functions, improving survival and quality of life.
kidney_transplant.what_is_para3: Unlike dialysis, which only partially replaces kidney function, a successful transplant allows patients to live a more active and normal life.
kidney_transplant.why_needed_title: Why is a Kidney Transplant Needed?
kidney_transplant.why_needed_para1: Doctors recommend a kidney transplant when kidney damage becomes severe and other treatments are no longer effective.
kidney_transplant.symptom2: Swelling in the legs, ankles, or face due to fluid retention
kidney_transplant.symptom3: Nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite
kidney_transplant.why_needed_para2: A transplant is usually considered when the <bold>glomerular filtration rate (GFR) falls below 20 mL/min, </bold>indicating severe kidney damage.
kidney_transplant.why_needed_note: Note: Better to send us your medical reports and we will confirm with a doctor whether you need a transplant or not.
kidney_transplant.indications_Des: Several medical conditions can make a patient eligible for a kidney transplant:
kidney_transplant.indication1: <bold>End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD):</bold> Loss of over 90% of kidney function.
kidney_transplant.indication2: <bold>Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD): </bold>Stage 4 or 5 CKD due to diabetes, hypertension, or polycystic kidney disease.
kidney_transplant.indication3: <bold>Acute Kidney Injury (AKI): </bold>Severe sudden kidney failure that does not recover.
kidney_transplant.indication4: <bold>Congenital Kidney Disorders: </bold>Structural abnormalities present since birth.
kidney_transplant.indication6: <bold>Autoimmune Diseases: </bold>Conditions like lupus or vasculitis causing kidney damage.

heart_transplant_implant.title: Advanced Heart Implants & Transplants | InDocsCare Medical Services
heart_transplant_implant.intro_para1: At <bold>InDocsCare,</bold> we offer cutting-edge solutions for patients with advanced heart failure — including <bold>Heart Transplants</bold> and <bold>Left Ventricular Assist Devices (LVADs)</bold>.
heart_transplant_implant.intro_para2: When heart transplant isn’t immediately possible or a donor isn’t available, LVAD implants provide life-saving support. These mechanical heart pumps help your heart circulate blood, improve organ function, and restore your quality of life.
heart_transplant_implant.what_is_para1: An<bold> LVAD (Left Ventricular Assist Device)</bold> is a mechanical heart pump that helps patients with <bold>advanced heart failure.</bold> It supports your heart in pumping blood, improving circulation and enhancing quality of life.LVAD is not a heart replacement — your heart continues to work along with the device.
heart_transplant_implant.use1: <bold>Bridge to transplant: </bold>Keeps patients alive while waiting for a donor heart.
heart_transplant_implant.use2: <bold>Bridge to recovery:</bold> Supports heart recovery, possibly avoiding transplant.
heart_transplant_implant.use3: <bold>Destination therapy:</bold> Provides long-term support for patients not eligible for transplant.
heart_transplant_implant.how_it_works_para1: The device is surgically implanted and connected to your heart and aorta. It is powered externally and controlled through a small controller unit.Post-surgery, patients typically experience <bold>more energy, improved mobility</bold>, and<bold> better quality of life</bold>. Most can return to normal activities, work, or school.
heart_transplant_implant.risks_para1: As with any surgery, risks include bleeding, infection, and device malfunction — but modern LVADs are highly reliable.Patients and families receive full training on device management.
heart_transplant_implant.notes: <bold>Note:</bold> Contact us at InDocsCare and we will assist you step by step in getting back to your healthy heart.
